WRITING TIME: 40 MINUTES

Read the case notes below and complete the writing task which follows.

Your patient, an 81-year-old woman, recently had a right total knee replacement (R.TKR) on 25/02/2015.
She is being discharged today. ‘

Patient:

Address:

Marital Status:

Past Medical History:

Ms Betty Johnson
12 Merry Street, Stillwater
Widowed

Aortic valve replacement & pacemaker 2010
Osteoarthritis since 2011 — pain & immobility 7 past 3yrs
For R.TKR Feb 2015: full blood work, typing & cross matching, X-rays, ECG etc.

Regular Medication (25/2/15):

Social Background:

Post Op:
25/02/15 11:30am

Paracetamol 665mg 2 tabs tds
Warfarin 3mg mane — ceased 5 days preoperatively, started Clexane
(enoxaparin sodium — anticoagulant)

Widowed 1986. Lives alone. 4 children

Retumed to ward following R. TKR.

Vital signs — BP 115/70, P 82, R 16, T 36.9°C.

Circulation observation good, knee T on pillow.

Hb 80g/I > IVT Transfusion.

1V cephalothin 1g qid for 24 hours.

Increase regular oral paracetamol (1g qds).

Patient Controlled Analgesia (PCA) — morphine v effective.
Wound — nil ooze.

26/02/15 Wound — good, sponged.
Restart warfarin 5mg today.
s/c Clexane 80mg given for anticoagulation.
Cease PCA, Start oxycodone 5 — 10mg pm.
Pathology: FBE, U&Es, Liver Function Tests (LFTs), Hb.
. Path results “, Hb 100g/ > commence Feratab (iron sulphate) 300mg mane.
27/02/15 s/c Clexane 80mg.
Start warfarin 5mg nocte.
Removal of (R/O) dressing, wound good, R/O alt. clips on 03/03/15.
28/02/15 Crutches, short walks, Wound good, afebrile.
s/c Clexane 80mg given.
01/03/15 s/c Clexane 80mg given.
02/03/15 X-rays, bloods “, INR — 3.0, Hb 111g/, ECG — no abnormalities.
Managing w/ min assistance.
Cease Clexane.
03/03/15-05/03/15 Wound clean, R/O alt clips tomorrow. Mobility good. Obs ”.
06/03/15 R/O remaining clips. Pathology ”. Transfer to rehab today.
Rehab:
07/03/15 Admission complete — stable. Circ /. Mobility, crutches good.
08/03/15-13/03/15 Mobility, frame use, trial stick, pool, gentle exercises = good. Showering w/ min
assistance.
Path & X-ray.
14/03/15 Path /, INR —3.8. ‘
warfarin 4mg nocte, Hb — 112g/, \ Feratab 150mg mane.
15/03/15-19/03/15 Uneventful — gradually T independence.
Wound good, Obs /. Physio exercises good. Home list provided.
21/03/15 No cardiac issues.

Discharged w/ home nursing assistance (personal hygiene, home care). Wound
exposed, shower w/ min assist. Stick / frame prn.

Discharge medication: warfarin 4mg nocte, Feratab 150mg mane, paracetamol
1g qds, oxycodone 5-10mg prn.

Rehab appt in 2 weeks.

Advised to see local doctor in 1 week, referral for local doctor — suggest repeat
FBE, INR.

Using the information given in the case notes, write a letter of referral to Ms Johnson's local doctor,
Dr Tony Jones, to update him on her condition following her recent surgery and discharge from rehab.
Address the letter to Dr Tony Jones, Private Practice, 12 New Street, Stillwater.

+ Use letter format
